items.title: 68189_Al Hall oral history interview
items.q: INTERVIEWER mentions Miles Davis as an example of someone who came out of the Charlie Parker/Dizzy Gillespie period; Interviewee responds only to the general context of money and leadership, not indicating a personal connection.

ctx.x: He's a beautiful player, though. Don't get me wrong. He sounds nice, his whole band. But they haven't got any leaders that could get a job out of any of these bands, a Black person put in charge.
Well, some players did come out of, you know, talking -- going back to that era -- come out of the Charlie Parker, Dizzy Gillespie, you know, period, who did go on to become like Miles Davis.
